question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


Give me / a book / that is / on the table.
options:
on the table

Give me

a book

that is
solution:
Given sentence:

Give me / a book / that is / on the table.

Issue:

  • Using “a book” implies any book, not a specific one.

  • But the relative clause “that is on the table” refers to a specific book.

  • Therefore, the correct article should be “the book” (definite article) instead of “a book” (indefinite article).

Correct sentence:

Give me / the book / that is / on the table.

Explanation:

  • “a” → indefinite article, used when talking about any one of a type.

  • “the” → definite article, used when referring to a specific item already identified or described.

  • Since the book on the table is specific, “the book” is grammatically correct.

Hence, the segment containing the error is:
2. “a book” → should be “the book.”

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

By this time tomorrow, / you will be playing / the violin / for 48 hours.
options: you will be playing
By this time tomorrow,
the violin
for 48 hours
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "you will be playing"

Explanation:
☛ The given sentence requires Future Perfect Continuous Tense as it indicates an ongoing action that will continue up to a specific future time.
☛ "you will be playing" uses Future Continuous Tense, which is incorrect because the action spans a duration (48 hours).
☛ The correct phrase should be: "you will have been playing" to accurately reflect the duration.
☛ With time reference (By this time tomorrow) and duration (for 48 hours), Future Perfect Continuous Tense is mandatory.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Future Perfect Continuous Structure: will/shall + have been + V1+ing is used for actions that will continue up to a specific future time.
☛ Key indicators: Words like for, since, by the time often accompany this tense.
☛ Difference: Future Continuous (will be playing) shows ongoing future actions, while Future Perfect Continuous emphasizes the duration of the action.

Example:
Incorrect - By next month, she will be studying for 5 hours.
Correct - By next month, she will have been studying for 5 hours.

Solution: Correct Answer is "five miles were not"

☛ Distance, time, and measurement units take singular verbs when referred to as a whole. Example: Twenty dollars is a fair price.
☛ The correct phrase should be: five miles was not, as the focus is on the collective distance.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Use singular verbs with measurements (distance, weight, time) when they represent a single idea. Example: Two hours is the duration.
☛ For individual units, use plural verbs. Example: The miles were counted separately.
☛ Pay attention to subject-verb agreement rules in competitive exams, especially with collective nouns and measurements.

Example:
Incorrect - Ten kilograms are heavy.
Correct - Ten kilograms is heavy.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Mr. Ramesh and / his friends / have never come / here
options: here
Mr. Ramesh and
have never come
his friends
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "have never come"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in the segment "have never come" because the subject (Mr. Ramesh and his friends) is plural, but the present perfect tense is used where the auxiliary verb "has" is used for singular subjects and "have" is used for plural subjects.
☛ Here, "his friends" combined with "Mr. Ramesh" forms a plural subject, so the use of "have" is correct. However, after "never," the correct form is "come" (past participle).
☛ Thus, there is no error in the sentence. All given options are correct, but from an exam perspective, this question is designed to confuse students.

Grammar Rules:
☛ In Present Perfect Tense, has/have + past participle is used.
☛ Use "has" with a singular subject and "have" with a plural subject.
☛ Adverbs of frequency (e.g., never, always) are placed between the auxiliary verb and the main verb.
☛ The past participle form of "come" is "come" itself; "came" is used in the past simple.

Example:
Incorrect - She have never went there.
Correct - She has never gone there.

Solution: Correct Answer is "who are"

☛ The erroneous segment in the given sentence is "who are".

☛ The relative pronoun "who" can refer to both singular/plural antecedents, but its verb must agree with the antecedent.
☛ "A pet dog" being a singular noun requires a singular verb "is".
☛ This error falls under the Subject-Verb Agreement rule.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Verbs following relative pronouns (who, which, that) must agree with their antecedents in number and person.
☛ Always use singular verb with singular subject.
☛ Always use plural verb with plural subject.
☛ Violation of this rule results in Subject-Verb Agreement error.

Example:
Incorrect - The boy who are my friend plays cricket.
Correct - The boy who is my friend plays cricket.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Modal verbs (will/shall/can/may) always take V1 after them.
☛ Example:

Correct - They will complete the task.
☛ Note: "By now" typically pairs with present perfect or future perfect, but here the context suggests simple future.

Grammar Rules:

☛ Present Perfect vs. Simple Past: Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is used for unspecified time, while Simple Past (V2) is used with specified time.
☛ Example:
Incorrect - He said that he has submitted the report last week.
Correct - He said that he had submitted the report last week.

☛ The suffix -ly is often used to form adverbs (e.g., brave → bravely).
☛ To modify a verb ("fought"), an adverb ("bravely") must be used.

Example:
Incorrect - He fought the lion brave.
Correct - He fought the lion bravely.

solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "brave"

Explanation:
☛ दिए गए वाक्य में "brave" शब्द का प्रयोग गलत तरीके से किया गया है।
☛ "Brave" एक adjective (विशेषण) है, जो किसी noun (संज्ञा) या pronoun (सर्वनाम) की विशेषता बताता है।
☛ यहाँ "fought" (क्रिया) के बाद "bravely" (क्रिया-विशेषण) का प्रयोग होना चाहिए, क्योंकि यह क्रिया की विशेषता बताता है।
☛ Adverb (क्रिया-विशेषण) क्रिया को modify करता है, न कि adjective (विशेषण)।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Adjective का प्रयोग संज्ञा या सर्वनाम के साथ होता है, जबकि adverb का प्रयोग क्रिया, विशेषण या दूसरे क्रिया-विशेषण के साथ होता है।
☛ -ly प्रत्यय का प्रयोग अक्सर adverbs बनाने के लिए किया जाता है (जैसे: brave → bravely)।
☛ वाक्य में क्रिया ("fought") को modify करने के लिए adverb ("bravely") का प्रयोग आवश्यक है।

Example:
Incorrect - He fought the lion brave.
Correct - He fought the lion bravely.
